title: Research evidence brief
summary: Turn supplied sources into a clear, traceable picture of what is known and what is still uncertain.
outcome: A source-linked brief with themes, disagreements, limitations, and useful next questions.
inputs: A research question or decision to inform
Source excerpts, documents, or notes with labels you can trace
starterPrompt: Use the research evidence brief skill to answer [question] using the supplied, labeled sources. Separate source-supported findings from interpretations and unknowns. Show agreements, disagreements, and limitations, and link each important claim to its source label. End with a concise brief and the next questions worth investigating. Do not invent sources or browse unless I ask. Ask for the question or source material if it is missing.
sampleInput:
Question: Should our internal help desk try a shared FAQ?
Source A, support log sample: 18 of 30 tickets ask how to reset access; this is one week from one team.
Source B, interviews: 3 of 5 employees could not find the existing guide. Two preferred asking a colleague.
Source C, operations note: The current guide has not been reviewed for six months. We do not have evidence about the time an FAQ would save.

title: Decision brief
summary: Compare real options against explicit criteria and make the tradeoffs easy to review.
outcome: An evidence-based comparison, open questions, and a conditional recommendation.
inputs: Decision criteria, priorities, and hard constraints
starterPrompt: Use the decision brief skill to compare [options] for [decision]. Apply my stated criteria and hard constraints. Build a comparison using only supplied evidence, distinguish missing information from a negative result, and make assumptions explicit. Explain tradeoffs and give a conditional recommendation with the questions that could change it. Do not invent weights, prices, or commitments. Ask for missing criteria before making a final recommendation.
sampleInput:
Decision: Pick a format for a 20-person internal workshop.
Criteria: Everyone must be able to join; budget limit is 5,000 THB; prefer interactive practice.
Option A: Onsite session costs 4,500 THB. Two remote colleagues cannot attend onsite.
Option B: Online session costs 1,000 THB and all colleagues can join. Breakout-room access is not confirmed.
Option C: Hybrid costs are not available. Remote participation quality has not been tested.

title: Presentation storyline
summary: Shape supplied facts into an audience-focused story before designing the slides.
outcome: A slide-by-slide outline with a clear message, supporting evidence, and speaker notes.
inputs: Source material or facts to communicate
The audience, intended decision, and presentation length
starterPrompt: Use the presentation storyline skill to outline a presentation for [audience] that helps them [decision or next action]. Use the supplied material as the factual basis. Give each slide one message, the supporting evidence, a suggested visual, and short speaker notes. Mark unsupported claims and missing figures. Deliver a text outline ready for review; do not claim to have created a slide file. Ask for the audience and intended outcome if they are missing.
sampleInput:
Audience: Operations leadership.
Outcome: Approve a two-week test of a clearer request form.
Length: Five slides in five minutes.
Facts: In a sample of 40 requests, 12 needed follow-up for missing information. The current form has one free-text field. A proposed form asks for deadline, owner, and requested output. We have not tested whether it reduces follow-up. The test would use one team and compare the next 40 requests with the initial sample.

title: Meeting follow-through
summary: Turn meeting notes into a grounded recap, clear actions, and an unsent follow-up draft.
outcome: Decisions, action items, unresolved questions, and a message ready for human review.
inputs: The meeting date and intended audience, if known
starterPrompt: Use the meeting follow-through skill with these meeting notes. Separate confirmed decisions, explicit actions, proposals, and open questions. Record owners and deadlines only where stated; keep uncertain or relative dates visible when the meeting date is missing. Draft a short follow-up for [audience] and flag anything that needs confirmation. Keep the draft unsent and do not update records or assign work.
sampleInput:
Notes from an internal planning call; meeting date not recorded.
Maya: I will draft the revised request form by Friday.
Lee: We could test it with the support team, but I need to check their availability.
Group decision: Keep the current form running during any test.
Someone suggested a two-week pilot; no start date was agreed.
The team needs a reviewer for the pilot results; no owner was assigned.
Audience: The internal project team.

title: Workflow improvement
summary: Map a real process, find its friction, and propose one bounded improvement to test.
outcome: A current-state map, evidence-backed pain points, and a small improvement experiment.
inputs: The current steps, roles, and handoffs
A pain point and any examples, constraints, or observations
starterPrompt: Use the workflow improvement skill to review [process] from the supplied steps, roles, and examples. Separate observed friction from hypotheses. Map the current handoffs, identify the smallest useful change, and describe a bounded trial with inputs, exceptions, owner to confirm, and a success measure. Do not invent time savings or implement changes. Ask for missing process steps before proposing a complete redesign.
sampleInput:
Process: A requester sends a free-text email. An administrator copies it into a tracker. The team lead assigns an owner. The owner replies when the work is complete.
Observed problem: In 12 of the last 40 requests, the administrator had to ask for the deadline or expected output before assigning work.
Constraint: Keep email as the entry point and use the existing tracker.
Goal: Reduce clarification messages without making the form difficult to use.

title: Reusable workflow blueprint
summary: Describe a recurring task as a reusable sequence with clear inputs, decisions, and checks.
outcome: A reviewable workflow blueprint with validation steps and unproven assumptions labeled.
inputs: A working example, runbook, or description of a recurring task
Expected output, decision points, and known constraints
starterPrompt: Use the reusable workflow blueprint skill to describe [recurring task] using my example or runbook. Identify the trigger, required inputs, ordered steps, decision points, exceptions, expected output, and verification checks. Preserve demonstrated behavior and label any proposed steps that have not been tested. Return a text blueprint for review. Do not claim to install, run, or validate an integration, and do not invent working commands.
sampleInput:
Recurring task: Prepare a weekly support recap.
Current example: Copy counts from the supplied weekly tracker, group open items by category, highlight items waiting for a reply, and draft a paragraph for the team.
Checks used last week: Compare totals with the tracker and confirm each highlighted item still has an open status.
Constraint: Do not contact requesters or publish the recap automatically.
Unknown: We have not tried this process when the tracker is incomplete.
